note: Covers both national branches. Ecuador: the Dúo Ecuador's 1930s records, Carlota Jaramillo 'La Reina del Pasillo', the Dúo Benítez-Valencia, Julio Jaramillo and Olimpo Cárdenas, the Hermanos Miño Naranjo (whose 'Tú y yo' won in Barcelona) and the modern revival of Juan Fernando Velasco and the Museo del Pasillo. Colombia: Jorge Villamil and José A. Morales pasillos sung by Garzón y Collazos and Silva y Villalba, and the instrumental pasillos of Fulgencio García and Luis A. Calvo played by Oriol Rangel. Release years are those on the store pages, mostly compilations and reissues, not first recordings; the Venezuelan vals and Central American pasillo are not represented.

size.basis: No source counts pasillo recordings; this is a judgement, not a count. Pasillo has been recorded for over a century in two main countries (Ecuador and Colombia) and more thinly in Venezuela (as vals), Panama and Central America. English Wikipedia (citing Benavides) says that in 1911, 67 of the 272 pieces recorded in Ecuador were pasillos; Nicasio Safadi's Dúo Ecuador recorded Guayaquil de mis amores and 37 other songs on 19 discs in New York on 19 June 1930. Single composers left hundreds of pasillos (Francisco Paredes Herrera 219, Carlos Vieco 273), and Julio Jaramillo alone made more than 200 45 rpm discs from 1956 to 1960, besides LPs titled for pasillos. Colombian duets (Garzón y Collazos, 216 songs; Silva y Villalba; Dueto de Antaño) and string ensembles (Oriol Rangel) mixed pasillos with bambucos across dozens of LPs, and iTunes still shows a steady flow of new 'pasillo ecuatoriano' albums and singles (2020-2026). An insider's essential list is about 60 recordings, split between the Ecuadorian sung pasillo (Dúo Ecuador, Carlota Jaramillo, Benítez-Valencia, Julio Jaramillo, Olimpo Cárdenas, Miño Naranjo) and the Colombian vocal duets and instrumental pasillo fiestero.
